readings.title: A Lament Over Defiled Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: The nations have desecrated the temple and made the people a reproach.
readings.text: [Psalm 79:1] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, the nations have come into <dn>Your</dn> inheritance; They have defiled <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Hěḵal; They turned Yerushalayim into ruins. [2] They have given the dead bodies of <dn>Your</dn> servants As food for the birds of the heavens, The flesh of <dn>Your</dn> lovingly-committed ones to the wild beast of the earth. [3] They have poured out their blood Like water all around Yerushalayim, With no one to bury them. [4] We have become a reproach to our neighbours, A scorn and a mockery to those who are around us.

readings.title: How Long, O YeHoVaH?
readings.subtitle: A plea for God to turn His wrath from His people to the nations who devoured Jacob.
readings.text: [Psalm 79:5] How long, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Would <dn>You</dn> be enraged forever? Would <dn>Your</dn> jealousy burn like fire? [6] Pour out <dn>Your</dn> wrath on the nations Who have not known <dn>You</dn>, And on reigns that have not called on <dn>Your</dn> Name. [7] For they have devoured <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ, And laid waste his pasture.

readings.title: A Prayer for Deliverance and Vengeance
readings.subtitle: Help us for Your Name's sake, and repay our enemies for their reproach.
readings.text: [Psalm 79:8] Do not remember against us The crookednesses of the fathers! Let <dn>Your</dn> compassion speedily meet us, For we have been greatly weakened. [9] Help us, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of our deliverance, For the sake of the esteem of <dn>Your</dn> Name. And deliver us, and cover over our sins, For <dn>Your</dn> Name’s sake! [10] Why should the nations say, “Where is their <dn>Elohim</dn>?” Let the vengeance of the outpoured blood of <dn>Your</dn> servants Be known among the nations, Before our eyes. [11] Let the groaning of the prisoner come before <dn>You</dn>. According to the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> arm Preserve those appointed to death. [12] And repay to our neighbours sevenfold Their reproach, into their bosom, With which they have reproached <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And we, <dn>Your</dn> people and the sheep of <dn>Your</dn> pasture, We give thanks to <dn>You</dn> forever; From generation to generation we show forth <dn>Your</dn> praise.

readings.title: Give Ear, O Shepherd of Israel
readings.subtitle: A call for God to shine forth and save His people.
readings.text: [Psalm 80:1] Give ear, O Shepherd of Yisra’ěl, Who leads Yosěph like a flock; Who dwells between the keruḇim, shine forth! [2] Before Ephrayim, Binyamin, and Menashsheh, Stir up <dn>Your</dn> might, And come and save us! [3] Cause us to turn back, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, And cause <dn>Your</dn> face to shine, That we might be saved!

readings.title: The Bread of Tears
readings.subtitle: Lamenting God's wrath and the mockery of their enemies.
readings.text: [Psalm 80:4] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, How long shall <dn>You</dn> be wroth Against the prayer of <dn>Your</dn> people? [5] <dn>You</dn> have caused them to eat the bread of tears, And have caused them to drink With tears, a third time. [6] <dn>You</dn> have made us a strife to our neighbours, And our enemies laugh among themselves. [7] Turn us back, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, And cause <dn>Your</dn> face to shine, That we might be saved!

readings.title: The Vine Brought from Egypt
readings.subtitle: Israel is pictured as a vine that once flourished but is now broken down and ravaged.
readings.text: [Psalm 80:8] <dn>You</dn> brought a vine out of Mitsrayim; <dn>You</dn> drove out the nations, and planted it. [9] <dn>You</dn> cleared a place for it, And caused it to take deep root, And it filled the land. [10] Hills were covered with its shadow, And the mighty cedars with its twigs. [11] She spread her branches to the Sea, And her shoots to the River. [12] Why have <dn>You</dn> broken down her hedges, So that every passer-by plucked her fruit? [13] The boar out of the forest ravages it, And the wild beast of the field devours it.

readings.title: Visit This Vine
readings.subtitle: A plea for God to restore His vine and strengthen the Son of Man at His right hand.
readings.text: [Psalm 80:14] Return, we beg <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts; Look down from heaven, and see, And visit this vine, [15] And the stock which <dn>Your</dn> right hand has planted, And the Son whom <dn>You</dn> made strong for <dn>Yourself</dn>. [16] It is burned with fire, it is cut down; They perish at the rebuke of <dn>Your</dn> face. [17] Let <dn>Your</dn> hand be upon the One at <dn>Your</dn> right hand, Upon the Son of Aḏam whom <dn>You</dn> made strong for <dn>Yourself</dn>, [18] And we shall not backslide from <dn>You</dn>. Revive us, and let us call upon <dn>Your</dn> Name. [19] Turn us back, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, And cause <dn>Your</dn> face to shine, That we might be saved!

readings.title: A Call to Festive Worship
readings.subtitle: Shout for joy and blow the shophar, for it is a law for Israel.
readings.text: [Psalm 81:1] Shout for joy to <dn>Elohim</dn> our strength; Raise a shout to the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‛aqoḇ. [2] Lift up a song and beat the tambourine, The pleasant lyre and with the harp. [3] Blow a shophar in the New moon, in the covering for the day of our festival. [4] For this is a law for Yisra’ěl, And a right-ruling of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‛aqoḇ. [5] <dn>He</dn> appointed it in Yehosěph for a witness, When <dn>He</dn> went throughout the land of Mitsrayim; <dn>I</dn> heard a language that <dn>I</dn> did not know.

readings.title: The Voice of Elohim: Deliverance and Warning
readings.subtitle: God recounts His deliverance of Israel from Egypt and commands them to have no other gods.
readings.text: [Psalm 81:6] <dn>He</dn> says, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> removed his shoulder from the burden; <dn>His</dn> hands were freed from the baskets.</dq> [7] <dq>“<dn>You</dn> called in distress, and <dn>I</dn> rescued you; <dn>I</dn> answered you in the covering of thunder; <dn>I</dn> proved you at the waters of Meriḇah. Selah.</dq> [8] <dq>“Hear, O <dn>My</dn> people, and let <dn>Me</dn> warn you, O Yisra’ěl, if you would listen to <dn>Me</dn>!</dq> [9] <dq>“Let there be no strange mighty one among you, And do not bow down to a foreign mighty one.</dq> [10] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, Who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim; Open your mouth wide, and <dn>I</dn> fill it.</dq>

readings.title: The Voice of Elohim: Israel's Stubbornness
readings.subtitle: God laments that His people would not listen, promising victory and provision if they would walk in His ways.
readings.text: [Psalm 81:11] <dq>“But <dn>My</dn> people did not listen to <dn>My</dn> voice, And Yisra’ěl would not submit to <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [12] <dq>“So <dn>I</dn> gave them over to their own stubborn heart, To walk in their own counsels.</dq> [13] <dq>“O, if <dn>My</dn> people had listened to <dn>Me</dn>, Yisra’ěl would walk in <dn>My</dn> ways,</dq> [14] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> would subdue their enemies at once, And turn <dn>My</dn> hand against their adversaries!</dq> [15] <dq>“Those who hate <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would cringe before <dn>Him</dn>; And their time of punishment be forever.</dq> [16] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> would feed them with the finest of wheat; And with honey from the rock <dn>I</dn> would satisfy you.”</dq>

readings.title: God Judges the Judges
readings.subtitle: Elohim stands in the divine assembly and rebukes the 'elohim' for their perverse judgment.
readings.text: [Psalm 82:1] <dn>Elohim</dn> stands in the congregation of <dn>Ěl</dn>; <dn>He</dn> judges in the midst of the elohim. [2] How long would you judge perversely, And show partiality to the wrong? Selah. [3] Give right-ruling to the poor and fatherless, Do right to the afflicted and needy. [4] Rescue the poor and needy; Deliver them from the hand of the wrong.

readings.title: The Sentence of the Corrupt Rulers
readings.subtitle: Though called 'elohim' and sons of the Most High, they will die like men.
readings.text: [Psalm 82:5] They do not know, nor do they understand, They walk about in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken. [6] <dq><dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> said, “You are elohim, And all of you are sons of the Most High.</dq> [7] <dq>“But as men you die, And fall as one of the heads.”</dq> [8] Arise, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, judge the earth, For <dn>You</dn> shall possess all the nations.
